question: When University of California staff could look up colleagues' pay online, who became less satisfied, and who happier?
answer: Only those paid below their unit's median changed: they grew less satisfied and likelier to look for work. Those above it gained no happiness at all. Card, Mas, Moretti and Saez told a random group about a newspaper site listing every salary. Earning less than the next desk stings; earning more barely registers.
move: Upward comparisons cost more than downward ones pay; ration them.
ask: Whose salary, house or holiday do I keep checking, and does it ever leave me feeling better?
source: Card, Mas, Moretti & Saez, American Economic Review, 2012
reference: Card, Mas, Moretti & Saez, Inequality at work: the effect of peer salaries on job satisfaction, American Economic Review, 2012
